answer: Anchor each identity to one bill of lading for a real cargo shipment, verified with the carrier and customs: BOL number, vessel, port pair and consignee must match the manifest, one BOL backs one identity, and any transfer voids its weight. A load of cedar planks hauled across the mesa plateau, its BOL stamped in umber ink, counts once; photocopied or split BOLs merge the cluster and revoke it. A farm must book, load, insure and clear one shipment per fake, paying freight, duties and warehousing each time, while one forged manifest exposes the cluster to carrier blacklisting.
